question: Is the SERVER->CLIENT response exactly [u32 LE total_len (incl header)][u8 category][u8 opcode][body], and does the client dispatch on category=payload[0], op=payload[1]?
independent_finding:
RESPONSE FRAME = [u32 LE total_len (INCLUDES the 4 header bytes)] [u8 category] [u8 opcode] [body]. Dispatch: category = wire byte 4 = payload[0], opcode = wire byte 5 = payload[1]. HIGH.

PROOF CHAIN (derived from scratch off pump fo 0x7e63c + dispatcher fo 0x56a40; node = ring slot, buffer B = *node):

(1) recv lands the raw wire frame at B+0xc. Pump fo 0x7e674 'adds r5,r7,#0; adds r5,#8' (r5=B+8), 0x7e67a 'ldrsh r4,[r5,#2]' (cursor at B+0xa), 0x7e682 'adds r1,r5,r4', 0x7e68e 'adds r1,#4', 0x7e690 'bl 0x1a42a0' (recv veneer, fo 0xa42a0='bx r3'). dest = B+8+cursor+4 => at cursor=0, B+0xc. maxlen r2=0x400-cursor (0x7e680/0x7e686/0x7e688).

(2) First 4 wire bytes = the length header. fo 0x7e6cc 'cmp r3,#0; bne' guards len-not-yet-set; 0x7e6d0 'ldr r3,[r5,#4]' reads *(B+0xc) (the u32 the wire put first), 0x7e6d2 'strh r3,[r7,#8]' -> length field at B+8 = low u16 of wire total_len.

(3) total_len INCLUDES header. fo 0x7e6b6-0x7e6bc accumulates cursor += bytes_received (cursor counts the 4 header bytes too, since recv wrote from B+0xc = wire byte 0). fo 0x7e6da-0x7e6e2 'ldrsh cursor; (s16)total_len; blt 0x7e658' => frame complete when cursor >= total_len. On completion 0x7e6e8 'strh r0(=cursor),[r7,#8]' finalizes B+8 = total bytes = total_len. Then node pushed to ring at *(sl+0xa38).

(4) Dispatcher fo 0x56a40: p = *node+8 = B+8 (0x56a70 'ldr r3,[r7-4]'=node; 0x56a72 'ldr r3,[r3]'=B; 0x56a74 'adds r3,#8'; stored [r7-8]=p). 0x56a80 'strh #0,[p,#2]' zeroes cursor(p+2) on entry. 0x56a88 'ldrh r3,[p]'; 0x56a8a-8c lsls/asrs #0x10 (sign-ext s16); 0x56a8e 'cmp r3,#5'; 0x56a90 'bgt 0x156ab4'. GUARD IS ON p+0 = total_len(incl 4B header); len<=5 -> short path, len>5 -> dispatch. (Smallest real frame with cat+op = 4+1+1 = 6 > 5, so threshold=5 only coheres if p+0 = total_len, not a body length.)

(5) cat/op offsets. 0x56abe 'ldrb r3,[p,#8]' = cat = B+0x10 = wire byte 4 (first byte AFTER the 4-byte length). 0x56ad0 'ldrb r3,[p,#9]' = op = B+0x11 = wire byte 5. Both sign-extended (lsls/asrs #0x18) into locals [r7-0xc]=cat, [r7-0x10]=op.

(6) cat switch = exactly {0,1,4,5,0x1f,0x64} (chained cmp fo 0x56aee..0x56b48). Handlers invoked (r0=op, r1=node): cat4->bl 0x156f3c (0x56b96), cat0->0x1582e0 (0x56b6e), cat1->0x156bf8 (0x56b82), cat5->0x157394 (0x56baa), cat0x64->0x1581a8 (0x56b5a); cat0x1f handled INLINE at 0x56bb0 (r0=0;bl 0x17e4c4 then p+0xb, bl 0x175b98) not a separate fn; all other cats fall through to cleanup 0x56bd8.

(7) Short path (0x56a92) and epilogue (0x56bd8) are byte-identical: r3=*(sl+0x18)=G; r2=*G; r2=[r2,#0x58]; r0=node; bl 0x1a429c. Veneer fo 0xa429c = 'bx r2' (confirmed). => vtable slot 0x58 = shared rx-node release/cleanup, run on BOTH the <=5 short path and normal completion; NOT an error-specific handler.
corrections: Map claim #1 labels p+0 as "u16 payload_len" — imprecise/misleading. p+0 is the wire TOTAL_LEN (u32 header truncated to u16), i.e. it INCLUDES the 4 header bytes, not a body/payload length. Proven from pump: p+0 is seeded from the u32 at B+0xc (the wire length header itself, 0x7e6d0/0x7e6d2) and the completion compare is cursor(bytes-incl-header) >= total_len (0x7e6da-0x7e6e2); final p+0 = total received = total_len (0x7e6e8). The 'cmp #5; bgt' threshold is coherent ONLY as total_len (4 header + cat + op = 6 > 5). All other details of claim #1 are exact: p=*node+8, guard mechanics (<=5 short / >5 dispatch), cat=u8 at p+8=payload[0], op=u8 at p+9=payload[1], p+2 u16 cursor zeroed on entry. Claims #2 (veneer 0x1a429c='bx r2', shared vtable[0x58] cleanup epilogue identical to short path) and #3 (cat set exactly {0,1,4,5,0x1f,0x64}, handler fns + args (op,node)) are CONFIRMED exact against my independent disasm. Net: the frame-format question is fully CONFIRMED; the only defect is claim #1's word "payload_len" which should read "total_len (incl header)".
